questions.question: When driving in wet conditions, what does it mean if you see no spray from other vehicles?

options.text: Ice has formed on the road.
The spray is stuck under the vehicle.
The tires have absorbed all the water.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ice has formed on the road.
questions.explanation: If the road looks wet but other vehicles are not spraying water, ice has formed on the road. Drive carefully on wet or icy roads.

questions.question: ____ is a thin layer of ice that forms on road surfaces.
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice. You can see the road through it. A road with black ice looks wet, not icy. Watch for black ice when a road looks wet and the temperature is near freezing.

questions.question: If another driver is tailgating your large vehicle, do all of the following except:

options.text: Keep more distance between you and the car ahead.

questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you, increase your distance from the car ahead and avoid sudden movements. Speeding up will only make the other driver tailgate you faster. Do not flash your brake lights or turn on your taillights at the other driver.

questions.question: Using a helper when backing up a large vehicle is:
questions.explanation: Backing a large vehicle is always dangerous because you have limited visibility. Using a helper to watch your blind spots is a good idea whenever possible.

questions.question: On a basic vehicle control skills test, you may be asked to:

options.text: Drive straight into a parking space.

questions.explanation: The basic vehicle control skills test may include straight line backing, offset back/right parking, offset back/left parking, driver side parallel parking, conventional parallel parking, and alley docking.

questions.question: If you stop on the side of the road, how should you warn other drivers?

options.text: Turn on your four-way emergency flashers.
Keep the driver's side door open.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your four-way emergency flashers.
questions.explanation: If you must stop on the side of the road, turn on your four-way emergency flashers to warn other drivers.

questions.question: If you do not know the area where you need to back up, you should:

options.text: Get out and walk around to learn the area before backing up.
Not use both mirrors because it causes too much distraction.
Wait for someone else to back up first so you can watch.
Turn on your high beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out and walk around to learn the area before backing up.
questions.explanation: Backing is always dangerous because you cannot see everything behind your vehicle. If you do not know the area, get out and walk around to see your path before you back up.

questions.question: An example of required emergency equipment is:
questions.explanation: All commercial vehicles must have emergency equipment. This includes spare electrical fuses, three red reflective triangles or six fuses or three liquid burning flares, and at least one working fire extinguisher.

questions.question: What should you do if your brakes cannot build up hydraulic pressure?

options.text: Push the brake pedal down as hard as you can.

questions.explanation: If your hydraulic brakes will not build pressure to slow or stop your vehicle, try shifting into a lower gear, pumping the brakes, and/or using the emergency brake.

questions.question: Distracted driving can be caused by:
questions.explanation: Distractions while driving can be physical (like reaching for something), mental (like talking to a passenger), or both (like holding a phone to text).

questions.question: A distracted driver:

options.text: Usually cannot see or think as quickly.
Is usually aware of what is happening around them.
Is a good person to follow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually cannot see or think as quickly.
questions.explanation: Distracted driving causes slower thinking, delayed decisions, and poor actions. Watch for distracted drivers and stay away from them when you can.

questions.question: Backing with a trailer is dangerous because:

options.text: It is hard to see behind the vehicle.
Most trucks cannot move in reverse.
Cargo may fall out of the trailer.
There may be extra weight in the front of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is hard to see behind the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Backing up is dangerous because you cannot see everything behind your vehicle. If you must back up, use a helper if possible.

questions.question: What is the best advice for driving in fog?
questions.explanation: Driving in fog is dangerous and should be avoided if possible. If you must drive in fog, turn on your low beam headlights and fog lights, even during the daytime.

questions.question: Before driving a bus that has been parked for a few days, you should:

options.text: Assume the interior is in good working order.
Walk through the bus to check for any damage since the last trip.
Ask passengers to check the inside of the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk through the bus to check for any damage since the last trip.
questions.explanation: Unattended buses can be damaged. Before driving a parked bus, check the inside to make sure everything is in good condition.

questions.question: When making a tight maneuver, you should:

options.text: Not use your mirrors because they can distract you.
Use your mirrors, but not often.

questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often when making tight maneuvers.

questions.question: When driving a bus with passengers, you should:

options.text: Fuel the bus while passengers are on board.

questions.explanation: Bus drivers should not talk to passengers to avoid distractions. Do not fuel a bus while passengers are on board. Do not tow or push a disabled bus with passengers inside, unless it is unsafe for them to leave the bus.

questions.question: Move over laws require drivers approaching a stopped emergency vehicle to:

options.text: Move to a different lane away from the stopped vehicle.
Move to the far side of their lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to a different lane away from the stopped vehicle.
questions.explanation: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is stopped on a multilane road, drivers must move out of the lane next to it if they can do so safely. If moving over is unsafe, slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.question: When using your mirrors, you should check your tires to:

options.text: Watch for fires in the tires.
See if the tires are rolling properly.
See if the tread is sufficient.
Compare tire size to other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for fires in the tires.
questions.explanation: Check your tires regularly in your mirrors to notice tire fires. Tire fires can happen when tires are under-inflated, when dual tires touch, or when tires overheat.

questions.question: Rust around wheel nuts may mean:

options.text: The tires need to be replaced.

questions.explanation: Rust around wheel nuts may mean they are loose. Check that the nuts are tight if you see rust in that area.

questions.question: Stopping distance can be affected by:
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on how fast you are driving. The faster you go, the longer it takes to stop.
